label: Тихий / Громкий
description: Тихий vs громкий: quiet/loud contrasts across genders and everyday scenes.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Громкий' takes the masculine ending to match 'телевизор'. The everyday annoyance anchors the form in daily life.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Тихая' takes the feminine ending to match 'комната'. The library scene fits the quiet sense of the adjective naturally.

Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Тихое' takes the neuter ending to match 'место', here in its calm sense alongside 'спокойное'. The pairing shows тихий can mean peaceful as well as quiet.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Громкие' takes the plural ending to match 'звуки'. The street noise fixes the plural form in a concrete scene.
Strategic focus: Direct masculine contrast. 'Громкий' is nominative for 'ребёнок' while 'тихого' is accusative for the animate 'соседа'. One sentence pairs loud against quiet.
Strategic focus: Comparative form. 'Тише' is the comparative of 'тихий' and stays the same for any gender. The polite request shows the comparative in a common command.
Strategic focus: Masculine instrumental in the predicate. After past-tense 'был', 'тихим' takes the instrumental ending to match 'голос'. This shows the быть-plus-instrumental pattern.
Strategic focus: Plural instrumental in the predicate. After 'были', 'громкими' takes the plural instrumental ending to match 'аплодисменты'. The sentence extends the pattern into the plural.
Strategic focus: Comparative of the opposite adjective. 'Громче' is the comparative of 'громкий' and is invariable. The urgent request roots the form in everyday speech.
Strategic focus: Adverbial short form. 'Тихо' works as a predicate describing the surroundings, the impersonal use of тихий. The morning scene shows its calm, quiet sense.
